recovery.definition: OpenSportCoach's recovery score, 0–100: five signals against your own 30-day usual, weighted HRV 40 %, resting HR 20 %, sleep vs need 25 %, respiration 10 %, skin temperature 5 %. At your usual, HRV and resting HR earn half their points, so a good ordinary morning scores about 65–75; 67 and up reads as recovered. A signal the watch didn't record hands its weight to the others.

strain.definition: The day's Garmin training load mapped onto 0–21 (21 × load / 250, capped).

sleep_performance.definition: Sleep time as a share of Garmin's sleep need for the night.

hrv.definition: Average HRV across the night, from your watch.

hrv_band.definition: Garmin's own balanced range for your HRV (its baseline), from the night's HRV summary.

hrv_weekly.definition: Garmin's 7-night HRV average — what its HRV status compares with the balanced band.

rhr.definition: Resting heart rate for the day, from your watch.

rhr_baseline.definition: Mean of the last 30 days' resting heart rate.

rhr_7d.definition: 7-day average: the mean of each day and the 6 before it, over the days with a reading (at least 4) — the trend the nightly numbers wobble around.

readiness.definition: Garmin training readiness, from the wake-up reading.

fitness.definition: Fitness: Garmin load averaged with a 42-day exponential weight.

fatigue.definition: Fatigue: Garmin load averaged with a 7-day exponential weight.

load.definition: Garmin training load: EPOC, from heart rate. It barely registers lifting — read strength by tonnage and sets, never with cardio in one number.

tonnage.definition: Σ weight × reps over every logged set, warm-ups included — they were lifted.

weight.definition: Body weight from your scale, via Garmin.

bump.definition: Your latest session at the programmed load hit the target reps on every planned set.

starved.definition: A program day not trained for more than 7 days.

watch_sync.definition: Compared with what was last verified on your watch — no Garmin call.

week_like_for_like.definition: This week up to its last finished day against last week up to the same day — never a part week against a whole one. Today counts once it logged a session and nothing planned for it is left.

week_planned.definition: Still to come this week: Garmin's calendar and the coach's off-watch plan. Minutes: a gym day's estimate from the program, a watch workout's own estimate, else your median time for that sport over its last five sessions (≈).

week_target.definition: The coach's weekly band for this number (program WEEK_TARGETS; cardio load from your profile). Without one the row only says how it moved.

sleep_need.definition: Garmin's sleep need for each night, averaged over the nights so far.

race_countdown.definition: Days to race day; the countdown shows from 8 weeks out.

race_easy.definition: An easy day before a race: no sprints, VO2 work, threshold work or tests, and no heavy legs. Easy aerobic work, mobility and a lighter upper-body gym day are fine.

race_taper.definition: A taper day before an A race: the volume comes down by about half over the taper, and short race-pace efforts stay in.

race_day.definition: Race day: the race, its warm-up and its fuelling, and nothing else.

race_recovery.definition: A recovery day after a race: no intensity, and no long ride or long run. Easy aerobic work and mobility, and a light gym day from the second day. After an A race, short intensity may come back once its no-intensity days are over.

fuel_band.definition: Carbohydrate during a session, by its length, how hard it is and the sport. Under an hour: none. 60–90 min: none if easy, about 30 g/h if hard. 90 min to 2.5 h: 30–60 g/h easy, about 60 hard. Over 2.5 h: 60–90 g/h of glucose and fructose. Runs take the lower half of each band; swims none. Sources: ACSM 2016; Jeukendrup 2014.

fuel_target.definition: The rate planned: the top of a hard session's band, the middle of an easy one's, never above what your gut is trained to (60 g/h until you say otherwise), plus 10 g/h on a gut-training session.

fuel_gut.definition: The most carbohydrate an hour you have taken in training without trouble. Raised 10 g/h at a time, only after a logged session at the current rate.

fuel_taken.definition: What you logged taking, in grams, from each product's label and your bottle recipe as it was that day. Self-reported: Garmin does not record it.
